question.problem:
The vector $a$ is directed horizontally to the right and has magnitude $\sqrt{3}$, while the vector $b$ is directed vertically up and has magnitude $\sqrt{6}.$ Find a unit vector $u$ that is parallel to  $a+b$ and has the same direction as $a+b.$ 

Type $a$ and $b$ to represent the vectors $a$ and $b,$ respectively.  

$u=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we have to find $a+b.$ According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant $a+b$ goes from the tail of $a$ to the head of $b:$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14251721/assets/b7d45d7cd1ea2c61961da8279d3f8702d3e52092fc6aab75a94d3b5076928dba.png)

To find the unit vector corresponding to $a+b,$ we have to divide by the magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}{|a+b|}^{2} & ={|a|}^{2}+{|b|}^{2} \\  & ={(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{6})}^{2} \\  & =3+6 \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude is

$$
|a+b|=\sqrt{9}=3,
$$

and the corresponding unit vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a+b}{|a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(a+b).\end{aligned}
$$
